newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds pull back as RBA stays silent.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds pull back as RBA stays silent.

text.p: *Australian bonds pullback from their early highs after there was no rate cut annoucement from the Reserve Bank of Australia at 9.30 a.m.
*Attention now on retail trade, building approvals data.
Australian bonds pulled back after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) left monetary policy unchanged at its first window of opportunity to ease rates after Tuesday's board meeting.

Bonds were weakening from their early highs ahead of the 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time, and weakened further, with the short end moving into negative territory, when no change in policy was forthcoming.
However, the pull-back should be limited by expectations that the RBA will still cut rates sometime between now and early August, traders said.

Wednesday was not the favoured day in the market for a rate cut. Instead, Thursday, after the outcome of the U.S. FOMC meeting was known, or later in July after wages and inflation data were seen as more likely. A further possibility was a cut after the August 5 board meeting.
"This is probably going to persist for a number of weeks," Bankers Trust economist David Bassanese said of the speculation.

The focus has now turned to May retail trade and building approvals due at 11.30 a.m. Both series are expected to rise by two percent, but unexpected strength could see bonds extend their pull-back. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
